observation_summary: The method Period.normalizedStandard() unconditionally calls withYears() and withMonths() on a Period object. If the PeriodType does not support these fields, the underlying call to PeriodType.setIndexedField() throws an UnsupportedOperationException.
hypothesis: The method Period.normalizedStandard() fails because it attempts to call withYears() and withMonths() on a Period object without checking if the underlying PeriodType supports those fields.
prediction: The code in Period.normalizedStandard() lacks checks for type.isSupported(DurationFieldType.YEARS_TYPE) and type.isSupported(DurationFieldType.MONTHS_TYPE) before invoking withYears() and withMonths().
experiment_rationale: The provided snippet confirms that Period.normalizedStandard() performs logic to calculate years and months and then calls withYears/withMonths without any validation against the PeriodType, which is the direct cause of the UnsupportedOperationException observed in the stack trace.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a missing validation check. The code assumes that years and months can always be set on the resulting Period, but the PeriodType might not support these fields. Adding a check for field support before calling the setter methods is the correct fix.
